messages.content: You are a senior engineer choosing a technology stack. Read the project description and pick exactly one option per layer (frontend, backend, database, hosting) from the allowed lists. Use the id exactly as listed. Reply with one JSON object: {"frontend": "<id>", "backend": "<id>", "database": "<id>", "hosting": "<id>"}.

Allowed options (id = name):
frontend: nextjs = Next.js (React); react_spa = React SPA (Vite); nuxt = Nuxt (Vue); sveltekit = SvelteKit; angular = Angular; astro = Astro; htmx = Server-rendered HTML + HTMX; react_native = React Native (Expo); flutter = Flutter; native_mobile = Native iOS + Android (Swift / Kotlin)
backend: express = Node.js + Express; nestjs = Node.js + NestJS; fastapi = Python + FastAPI; django = Python + Django; go = Go (net/http, chi or Gin); spring_boot = Java/Kotlin + Spring Boot; dotnet = C# + ASP.NET Core; rails = Ruby on Rails; laravel = PHP + Laravel; phoenix = Elixir + Phoenix; serverless_functions = Serverless functions (Node/Python FaaS); supabase = Supabase (BaaS on Postgres); firebase = Firebase (BaaS on Google Cloud); no_custom_backend = No server code (static site)
database: postgres = PostgreSQL; mysql = MySQL; mongodb = MongoDB; dynamodb = Amazon DynamoDB; redis = Redis / Valkey; cassandra = Apache Cassandra / ScyllaDB; clickhouse = ClickHouse; opensearch = OpenSearch / Elasticsearch; neo4j = Neo4j; timescaledb = TimescaleDB (Postgres); sqlite = SQLite (+ Litestream backups); firestore = Cloud Firestore; none_static = No database (content files in git)
hosting: vercel = Vercel; netlify = Netlify; cloudflare = Cloudflare Pages + Workers; render = Render; railway = Railway; flyio = Fly.io; aws_ecs = AWS ECS on Fargate; aws_eks = AWS EKS (Kubernetes); aws_lambda = AWS Lambda + API Gateway; aws_s3_cloudfront = AWS S3 + CloudFront (static); gcp_cloud_run = Google Cloud Run; gcp_gke = Google Kubernetes Engine (Autopilot); azure_apps = Azure App Service / Container Apps; digitalocean = DigitalOcean (App Platform + Managed DBs); hetzner = Hetzner Cloud / VPS (Docker, Coolify); onprem_docker = On-prem VMs + Docker Compose; onprem_k8s = On-prem Kubernetes (k3s / RKE2 / OpenShift)

Project description:
We are a Berlin startup selling a project and timesheet management SaaS to European agencies and consultancies. Customers insist that all personal data is processed and stored inside the EU under GDPR, and that we can move providers if needed, so we want to avoid proprietary cloud services. The six of us are a Django and PostgreSQL team with React and TypeScript on the frontend, and we prefer one well-structured monolith. We expect 20,000 daily users within a year, 50 GB of data growing 10 GB a month, live notifications when tasks change, and about 3,000 USD a month for infrastructure.
